claims.claim: Didymus the Blind was born c. 313 in Alexandria, Egypt, and died c. 398 in Alexandria.
Didymus the Blind became entirely blind at age four and remained a layman all his life.
Didymus headed the influential catechetical school of Alexandria for about half a century.
Athanasius the Great, bishop of Alexandria, made Didymus head of the Alexandrian school.
Didymus was a student and faithful follower of Origen.
The treatise Against the Manichees was probably written by Didymus.
Manichaean missionaries were active in Egypt in the fourth century, disseminating their own account of the nature and origin of human evil.
The rise of the ascetic movement in fourth-century Egypt had focused attention upon the struggle against fleshly lusts and demonic powers.
Didymus's Contra Manichaeos is arguably the most important fourth-century Egyptian Christian response to Manichaean teachings about the origin of evil.
Didymus's exposure to and understanding of Manichaeism were limited, and he tended to confuse the views of the Manichaeans with those of earlier individuals and groups opposed by Origen.
The arguments in Contra Manichaeos demonstrate Didymus's indebtedness to Origen's theology and exegesis.
Didymus adhered to controversial aspects of Origen's theological anthropology, including the descent of preexistent souls into bodies soiled by sin and death.
SCOPE: this English is Contra Manichaeos, stored for didymus-contra-manichaeos. It is not a biblical commentary.
